rewrites.4F7BC4A5: Baselines are fixed at 2025, the growth model's base year, for the growth-model indicators and at FY2024/25 for the airport series, the recovery baseline used in Chapter 1. Targets follow two cases: the base case, which assumes Wesgro's current activity continues with hub carriers adding capacity, and the accelerated case, which adds direct India and China routes and dedicated activation. The model gives the base case for 2028, 2030, 2032, 2034 and 2035, and the other cases for 2035 only. The 2031 base value and the accelerated milestones are computed and marked as such.[^423]
rewrites.56CDB39E: Arrivals carry targets for both cases; spend carries the working analysis's base case; jobs, GDP contribution and the other Tier 1 indicators set baselines first.
rewrites.17BD7663: **Seats.** T2-09 and T2-10 are read against the seats the target requires. The 2.5 million target implies about 3.1 million inbound seats a year by 2035 and the base case about 2.7 million, against about 1.9 million in the year to November 2025 (section 2.4). The target and the base case need seat growth of about 5.1% and 3.6% a year. The figures are orders of magnitude, since arrivals and passengers are counted on different bases.
rewrites.134C36E2: **Jobs and GDP.** T1-04 and T1-08 take their baselines in 2027 from the economic measures workstream (I16), fed by the labour analysis (I18). DEDAT's 2023 figures for tourism are R28.6 billion in gross value added and over 257,000 jobs supported (section 2.5). The department publishes no method or definition with those figures, so they are a starting point and not yet a baseline. No tourism employment table appears in the PERO 2025 (section 3.3).[^426]
rewrites.1D5E635E: **Green season.** The 2025 month table sums to 104.9%. Normalised, it gives 61.9% for October to March and 38.1% for the green season, in line with the 61% and 39% reported for 2024. T1-05 uses 38.1% as its baseline. Absolute April to September nights and revenue are reported beside the share, because a share alone cannot show whether winter demand grew. The share has in fact slipped while volume grew: the airport series puts April to September at 41.6% of movements in 2023 and 40.8% in 2025. A share that rises because summer falls is not the intended gain.[^428]
rewrites.4916BC6E: **Spread and community spend.** No deliverable reports district visitor spend. The Provincial Treasury's district reviews give tourist spend as a share of GDPR, from 6.7% in the Metro to 16.8% on the West Coast in 2023. That measures tourism's weight in each district economy, not where provincial visitor spend lands. The share outside the Metro therefore takes its baseline from the data protocol in 2027 (I16), and T1-06 carries no interim level before then. The community share starts from the Inclusion Plan's traced floor; its 1% is a reference point that plan gives, not a target any party has adopted.[^429]
rewrites.28F657B5: Tracking uses a quarterly scorecard to Steerco, an annual outlook to the Board and a live dashboard where the sources allow it.
rewrites.0D8F75CD: Four principles run the tracking. Automation precedes collection by hand: arrivals, seats and cruise volumes come from feeds that already exist. The dashboard has one owner (the programme office) and the definitions have one (Wesgro Research). Every indicator is reported against its own baseline and both cases. The register is refreshed each year at the plan review.
rewrites.2C5CA953: Reporting runs on a fixed calendar tied to Steerco and the Board. Each month, the convenors send Tier 3 outputs, initiative status and the seats and arrivals feeds to the programme office as a dashboard update. Each quarter, the programme office takes Tier 2 outcomes where available, the risks rated high and the escalation responses to Steerco in the scorecard. Each year, Steerco takes Tier 1 impact against both cases, the plan refresh and gate status to the Board in an outlook report, made public at the business outlook event. At each gate, Steerco sends the Board a gate paper on the tests in section 4.7.
rewrites.31087294: The mid-term review tests whether the plan is on its path and whether the path still holds. It falls in 2030, before runway relief on the planning date, and tests seat growth against the path the target requires. The review also falls at the end of Wesgro's FY26 to FY30 plan period, in time to inform the next one. The terminal evaluation in 2035 measures the result against both cases and sets up the next plan. Both should be run by a party independent of the programme office.[^431]
rewrites.53228F7C: The four files are the indicator register, the baseline workbook, the scorecard template and the dashboard data model (SLA clauses 1.1.10.2 and 1.1.15.3). The indicator register holds all 80 indicators with their definition, unit, source, frequency, reporting unit or data holder, baseline and target by year and case. The baseline workbook holds the baseline values with page references to the deliverables, and the computed values with their method. Wesgro Research owns both. The programme office owns the scorecard template, which carries the quarterly Steerco scorecard and the annual Board outlook. It also owns the dashboard data model: the feeds, refresh frequency and manual-entry forms for the dashboard in section 5.5.
